messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failed test calls doTest("b:foo/test", MODEL_DOM, "/b:foo[1]/test[1]"). This creates a JXPathContext over a DocumentContainer reading XML file "InnerEmptyNamespace.xml" under the DOM model. Then it gets a pointer for the XPath "b:foo/test" and calls asPath() to verify the path string.

The current bug report states that resetting the default namespace (xmlns="") causes an endless loop when calling asPath() on such a node. The provided XML snippet in the report includes an element <test xmlns=""> which resets the default namespace. Calling asPath() on such an element triggers the bug.

The asPath() method is implemented in org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer for DOM nodes. Here, asPath() recursively calls parent.asPath() to build the full path. For elements, it tries to include prefix:localName[index]. If no prefix is found, it uses node()[index].

The endless loop likely happens because with xmlns="" (empty default ns), the namespace resolver returns null or behaves unexpectedly when DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI() is called. Then the code calls getNamespaceResolver().getPrefix(nsURI) with nsURI=null or empty and this returns null. Instead of producing a standard node path, it falls back to "node()" with an index. But possibly something in this logic causes it to re-call or fail to progress the recursion.

The recursion in asPath():
- calls parent.asPath() first
- then appends node info
If the parent is itself or returns the same pointer, an endless loop arises.

The bug is clearly in DOMNodePointer.asPath() logic handling elements with empty namespace (xmlns=""). The method does not correctly handle a reset default namespace that means no namespace. This can cause getNamespaceResolver().getPrefix(nsURI) to return null unexpectedly and fallback to node() + index, which might resolve incorrectly or cause an infinite recursion.

Thus, the root cause of the bug is: DOMNodePointer.asPath() does not correctly handle elements in no namespace (due to xmlns="") and that leads to infinite recursion when building the path string.

The test covers exactly this case and exposed the bug.

No recent bug reports with relevant info were found.

Summary:
- Test triggers asPath() on node with empty default namespace.
- DOMNodePointer.asPath() does recursive parent.asPath() + node suffix.
- For empty namespace elements, prefix lookup returns null.
- Falling back to node() + index likely triggers infinite recursion.
- Infinite recursion causes the test to fail as .asPath() hangs.

The bug should be fixed by improving DOMNodePointer.asPath() to correctly handle empty namespace elements without causing infinite recursion.

The main candidate method for fix is:
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.asPath()

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
